record.original_question: Is an arbitrary product of strong d-spaces again a strong d-space? Here a T0 space X is strong d if for every directed set D, point x, and open set U, whenever intersection_{d in D} (up d intersect up x) is contained in U, one already has up d intersect up x contained in U for some d in D.

evidence.quote: Question 8.10. Is the product space of an arbitrary family of strong d-spaces again a strong d-space?

Definition 8.1. A T0 space X is called a strong d-space if for any D in D(X), x in X and U in O(X), intersection_{d in D} up d intersect up x subseteq U implies up d intersect up x subseteq U for some d in D.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a $T_0$ topological space. For $x \in X$, write $\uparrow x = \{y \in X : x \le y\}$, where $\le$ is the specialization order of $X$ (i.e., $x \le y$ iff $x \in \overline{\{y\}}$). Let $\mathcal{D}(X)$ denote the collection of nonempty directed subsets of $X$ (directed with respect to $\le$), and let $\mathcal{O}(X)$ denote the topology of $X$.

Call $X$ a strong $d$-space if for every $D \in \mathcal{D}(X)$, every $x \in X$, and every $U \in \mathcal{O}(X)$,
$$\bigcap_{d \in D} (\uparrow d \cap \uparrow x) \subseteq U \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \uparrow d \cap \uparrow x \subseteq U \text{ for some } d \in D.$$

Question: Is the Tychonoff product $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ (in the category of topological spaces) of an arbitrary family $\{X_i\}_{i \in I}$ of strong $d$-spaces again a strong $d$-space?
artifact.status_search_result: Strong d-spaces, introduced by Xu and Zhao, have been studied in several follow-up works. A 2026 preprint on $S^*$-well-filtered spaces and $d^*$-spaces shows that products of $d^*$-spaces need not be $d^*$-spaces, and related results address strongly well-filtered spaces, but no source examined explicitly settles whether an arbitrary product of strong d-spaces is a strong d-space. The status appears to remain unresolved in publicly available sources.

status_evidence.title: S*-well-filtered spaces and d*-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: the product space of an arbitrary family of d*-spaces is not a d*-space ... an example to reveal that the product space of two d*-spaces is not a d*-space.
status_evidence.claim: Related products (of d*-spaces) are known to fail, but the question for strong d-spaces is not explicitly resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Strongly well-filtered spaces and strong d-spaces - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Strongly well-filtered spaces are closely related to well-filtered spaces and strong d-spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies strong d-spaces but accessible abstract does not confirm a resolution of the arbitrary-product question.
